requirements.requirement: Forward inventory-tagged application log messages from node2 to the centralized collector on node1.
requirements.summary: Node2 established a TCP forwarding session, emitted an inventory-tagged record, and node1 received it. A control record with an unrelated tag was correctly excluded.

requirements.requirement: Persist received messages on node1 at /var/log/inventory/node2.log.
requirements.summary: The required file existed on node1 and retained the inventory records across both restarts. Final evidence showed all three test records and root:adm mode 0640 metadata.

requirements.requirement: Keep log flow operational after either node1 or node2 restarts.
requirements.summary: Both nodes had directly observed restart transitions with changed boot identities. After node1 restarted, rsyslog, its listener, existing data, and a record submitted during the disruption recovered. After node2 restarted, rsyslog and its configuration recovered, the TCP session re-established, and a fresh inventory record reached node1. The fixed lifecycle boot identities independently agree with both transitions.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. Inventory-tagged messages flowed from node2 to node1, were persisted at the required path, and continued flowing after independently observed restarts of both systems. The provider-wide restart protocol was substantively complete for both nodes and consistent with the fixed lifecycle observations.
limitations: The functional tests generated inventory-tagged records with logger rather than capturing output from a separately observed inventory application process; this assumes the application emits standard syslog records with program name inventory.
The fixed failed-service lifecycle probe was unsupported on Alpine because it checks systemd, although direct OpenRC checks showed rsyslog healthy before and after each restart.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Installing rsyslog, creating its configuration and log directories, replacing the boot-enabled BusyBox syslog service, generating bounded test records, and restarting both nodes all had clear task or mandatory restart-evidence roles. The initially failed collector-config command created only the required log directory, which the final implementation retained and used. Temporary-file inventories and package-health results were unchanged, while the new TCP listener was required, bound to node1's managed address, and filtered by source and program name.
